sections.section_title: Without Love, the Most Impressive Gifts and Sacrifices Are Nothing
sections.summary: Paul argues that even the most exalted spiritual gifts (tongues, prophecy, all knowledge, mountain-moving faith) and the most radical acts of sacrifice (total distribution of possessions, surrender of the body) are worthless without love -- the person is noise, nothing, and gains nothing.

Paul describes love through fifteen behavioral predications -- patient, kind, not envious, not boastful, not arrogant, not rude, not self-seeking, not irritable, not resentful, not rejoicing at wrongdoing but with truth, bearing, believing, hoping, and enduring all things -- each functioning as a mirror exposing specific failures in the Corinthian community.

sections.section_title: The Permanence of Love and the Temporality of Gifts
sections.summary: Paul establishes that prophecy, tongues, and knowledge are temporary gifts belonging to the present age of partial understanding, which will be abolished when the complete arrives and the community moves from seeing through a mirror dimly to knowing God face to face.

Paul concludes that faith, hope, and love abide in the present age, but love is the greatest because it alone is not oriented toward what it lacks -- it is already the character of the consummated reality, while faith and hope will be transformed when their objects are fully present.
